_comment: Two Truths and a Fib: Retirement Edition. Each set is a short title and three statements on one topic: two true, one false (the fib), plus a one-sentence correction printed on the answer page. Variety is structural: every requested set gets its own brief (a subject domain and an angle, sampled by seed), so a reply cannot be eight versions of 'the telephone'. Nothing ships on the writer's word: a second, blind fact-check call judges every statement without being told which is the fib, and only a set it independently reads as true / true / false, with a true correction, survives. Length budgets arrive on the request (frontend/src/utils/studio/two-truths-and-a-fib/content.ts); limits below are the hard bounds. blockedTerms, timeTerms, absoluteTerms and hedgeTerms keep sensitive, dated, trick-worded and unverifiable claims off the page. qualifierWords are dropped and aliases folded before two statements are compared, so 'invented earlier than' and 'existed before' read as the same fact.

locale.nativeLine: - Write in clear, warm, natural English for adults and retirees. Avoid facts that only hold in one country unless the statement names the country.
locale.otherLine: - Write every title, statement and correction in language locale '{locale}', natural for that language. Avoid facts that only hold in one country unless the statement names the country.

levels.gentle: Gentle: familiar everyday subjects. The two truths are facts many adults half-remember; the fib is believable but a thoughtful reader can spot it.
levels.classic: Classic: interesting, lesser-known but well-documented facts. The fib is a believable detail -- a shifted date, a swapped place, a wrong material -- that takes a moment's thought.
levels.challenging: Challenging: surprising, well-documented facts that sound unlikely. The fib sounds at least as believable as the truths, yet is clearly false in any good reference book.

example.title: Lighthouse Lights
truths: The lighthouse at Alexandria in ancient Egypt was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
Many lighthouse lamps in the 1700s burned whale oil to make their light.
example.fib: The famous Fresnel lighthouse lens was invented in the 1920s.
example.fact: Augustin Fresnel invented his lighthouse lens in 1822.
